title: Gradient-Free Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision Models via Agentic Coding
read_level: partial (arXiv HTML v1: full main text Secs 1-6, Tables 1-3, LLM usage statement, Appendix E.4 cost; other supplements A-J not read)
why_wsp: A coding agent (Claude Opus 5.5; also GPT 6.1 Sol, Sonnet 5) inspects query embeddings and logits of a frozen COCO detector and writes a program that sets the new class rows and no-object row of its class head, under a prompt ban on gradients and least-squares fits, with a 25-pass evaluation budget.
facets: application domain: few-shot object detection / segmentation (vision)
domain: few-shot class addition to a detector/segmenter head (fine-grained cars, birds, pets, aircraft, satellite ships; also SAM 3, CLIP)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (main), GPT 6.1 Sol (second, three seeds), Claude Sonnet 5 (fails)
target: PMT mask transformer on frozen DINOv3 ViT-L; class head of K new rows (1024-dim) plus the no-object row; also SAM 3 and CLIP heads
interface: code/tensor tools (Python kernel holding editable tensors with gradients off; forward tool with generate/read/retain requests; agent also writes recipe.py that replays the edit)
loop: closed-loop with feedback ("Any request costs one of the B=25 passes"; up to C=300 code runs; COCO guard readout)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "The editable set holds the K new rows and the no-object row" (Sec 3.1); 80 stock rows untouched; K=10 classes per set.

headline_results.claim: Agent edit vs full-decoder FT at five shots
headline_results.quote: the Agent edit outperforms FT on CUB by 11.2 F1 points (95% interval 2.5-19.5) and on pets by 12.3 (1.0-23.3), in 4 and 4 of 5 seeds, respectively, and ties on cars and aircraft

headline_results.where: Table 1 (mean F1 / mean AP / COCO lost mean / worst run)

headline_results.claim: Outside-the-head classifier beats all in-head methods
headline_results.quote: a stock detector whose boxes a frozen DINOv3 classifier labels scores higher F1 than the Agent edit and the Agent formula on 5 of 5 sets
At ten shots no comparison with the mean FT order shows a gain for our methods

headline_results.claim: Parent-class AP drop in joint head
headline_results.quote: the AP of the COCO class to which the new classes belong ... falls by up to 33.3 points
Fine-tuning loses 47.3-51.4 points at five shots (Tab. 2), LwF 40.4-48.8.

headline_results.claim: Programs converge to a closed form
headline_results.quote: 166 of 243 independent programs contain all three, and 124 of 195 written after the formula was fixed
Sonnet 5 fails in the same harness, with F1 of 1.4-10.3 on all 15 cells against Opus's 18.7-93.2.
the edit raises F1 from zero to 75.1-79.0 at 20 shots, where Adam on the same tensors reaches 71.8 and a per-project trained head 84.9

cost.quote: An agent run on PMT takes 8.9-28.4 minutes of wall time and $1.59-$4.57 of model API cost per task.
The Agent formula needs 173-581 CPU seconds per cell and no GPU. FT with its grid needs 75.8-295.2 GPU minutes per cell

baselines_and_controls: Linear probe, imprinted cosine head, LwF, full-decoder FT (mean and best of three batch orders), TFA-style joint head, WiSE-FT, L2-SP, frozen-append gradient baseline in the same head under the COCO guard, CD-ViTO, nearest class mean, SimpleShot, shrinkage LDA (with the formula's gate), outside-the-head frozen-feature classifier, agent-written linear head on features, random edit of same size; prior-knowledge tests (names hidden, shuffled, invented classes, satellite ships).
runs_and_variance: "We run five seeds at 5 and 10 shots and three below 5 shots, at 20 shots and on ships"; two-level bootstrap over seeds and test images, 10000 resamples; "Across four Opus runs the standard deviation of F1 is 7.3 on cars and 6.3 on pets" (Sec 5).
robustness_of_edits: Forgetting measured as COCO mask mAP drop (mean 1.0, worst 5.5 at five shots); recipe.py replay across seeds and sets (partial transfer: 41.3-49.2 vs 54.2-74.8 live); cross-domain ArTaxOr/DIOR COCO loss 0.4-1.2. No fine-tuning or quantization survival tests.
verification: Static check rejecting gradient and network imports; logs audited for the fitting rule ("A scan of the logs finds a least-squares, pseudo-inverse, SVD or eigen-decomposition call in 54 of 54 audited runs, mostly for allowed statistics"); replay check that recipe.py reproduces the saved edit. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Hiding class names changes F1 by at most 3.7 points, shuffling by +3.4 to +4.7, 0 of 8 intervals exclude zero; invented classes and low-prior satellite ships tested; "we find no sign that prior knowledge of the classes explains the result". Authors also note the agent "recovers the standard nearest class mean classifier ... and does not exceed it" and that part of program overlap comes from the prompt.
limitations_stated: Outside-the-head classifier wins on 5/5 sets; gain disappears from ten shots; CD-ViTO exceeds on 2 of 5 sets; worst-run COCO drop 5.5 and parent-class AP drop up to 33.3; depends on agent model (Sonnet 5 fails); per-run variance; VLM classifies crops better; CLIP edits below best baseline.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog) [55], described as concurrent work
notes_for_survey: Vision-model WSP with gradient baselines on the same labels and explicit forgetting measurement. The agent's programs largely converge to a nearest-class-mean head with a gate and nuisance-direction removal, which the author distils into an agent-free 'Agent formula' that matches or beats the agent. Prompt bans least-squares fits, but LDA-style metrics appear in 25 of 243 independent programs.
